370.title: History and log print a missing old value as `None`
370.body: `python3 -m ledger history` shows the create entry as `None -> Jansen BV`.

comments.author: owner
comments.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Print an empty old value as `(empty)`

**Current behavior:** `show` in `ledger/__main__.py` formats `old_value` with an f-string, so a create row prints `None -> Jansen BV`.

**Desired behavior:** A missing old or new value prints as `(empty)`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A test runs `show` on a create row and finds `(empty) -> Jansen BV`.

**Out of scope:** anything else in `ledger/`.

371.title: Paginate Customer History by Audit Operation
371.body: Page the History tab by Audit Operation rather than by field row, so one edit never splits across pages.

comments.author: owner
comments.body:

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** `limit` on the History counts Audit Operations

**Current behavior:** `list_by_entity`'s `LIMIT` counts field rows, so an edit with many fields can be cut part-way.

**Desired behavior:** `limit` counts Audit Operations, built on the grouping from #372.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A test with limit 1 and a three-field edit gets all three fields.

**Out of scope:** anything else in `ledger/`.

372.title: Group audit rows into Audit Operations in list_by_entity
372.body: `list_by_entity` returns field rows; return one entry per Audit Operation with its fields.

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** `list_by_entity` returns Audit Operations

**Current behavior:** `list_by_entity` in `ledger/audit_store.py` returns one row per changed field.

**Acceptance criteria:**
